Change some settings of a step or a chain

Source: R/core-compose-step.R
hr_set.Rd

hr_set() builds a step or a chain again with some settings changed and the rest as they were. In a chain each setting is named by its path, "step.setting" (split at the first dot), as hr_settings() lists them: hr_set(chain, retrieve.top_k = 8). For a single step, the setting's own name is enough: hr_set(step, top_k = 8).

Usage

hr_set(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A step from hr_step(), gr_step() or gr_step_retrieve(), or an arm built by hr_chain().

...

The settings to change, each named: "step.setting" = value for a chain, setting = value for a single step.

Value

x built again with the settings changed: a step of the same class, or an arm from hr_chain() with the same name and version. With no settings given, x as it is.

Details

Only settings of a step's schema can be changed. A path whose step is not in the chain, or whose setting is not in that step's schema, is an error of class hr_unknown_setting (also hr_unknown_param and gr_bad_setting) that lists the settings of the step it names, or the steps of the chain. A setting the schema does not name, which a step built with build keeps as a fixed extra, is refused the same way.

The new values are checked by hr_validate() as when the step was built, so a number outside its range is moved to the nearest bound with a warning of class hr_param_clamped (also gr_clamped), and a value the step's constructor refuses, such as an unknown reader, is an error. Each step that changed is built again from its settings, through its build function when it has one, so a setting its constructor checks is checked here, and keeps its class: a gr_step() stays a gr_step.

The chain is then built again by hr_chain() under its own name and version, with the changed steps in place, so its hash and configuration are those of the new settings. A setting changed to its default gives the configuration of the chain with that setting left out. hr_sweep() calls hr_set() for each row of its grid when given a chain, which is how a chain is swept by name.

See also

hr_settings(), hr_sweep(), hr_chain(), hr_validate()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_condensation_check(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_reverse_text(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_chain(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_effort_check(), hr_effort_escalate(), hr_effort_event(), hr_effort_log(), hr_mdd(), hr_reference(), hr_report(), hr_scorer(), hr_settings(), hr_skill(), hr_step(), hr_step_command(), hr_sweep(), hr_sweep_check()

Examples

chain <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"),
                  retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 4),
                  read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"), name = "checked")
wider <- hr_set(chain, retrieve.top_k = 8, segment.max_tokens = 300)
wider$params
#> $segment.max_tokens
#> [1] 300
#> 
#> $retrieve.top_k
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $read.reader
#> [1] "stuff"
#> 
hr_settings(wider)[hr_settings(wider)$set, c("step", "param", "value")]
#>        step      param value
#> 2   segment max_tokens   300
#> 21 retrieve      top_k     8
#> 35     read     reader stuff

# A setting at its default is the chain without it.
six <- hr_set(chain, retrieve.top_k = 6)
plain <- hr_chain(chain, retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(), name = "checked")
identical(attr(six, "hr_config"), attr(plain, "hr_config"))
#> [1] TRUE

# A single step takes the setting's own name.
attr(hr_set(gr_step_retrieve(), top_k = 2), "resolved")$top_k
#> [1] 2
